raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
Split out of #8457.

## Problem
`get_node_shape_meta` in `deepspeed/compile/fx.py` picks between `meta["val"]` and `meta["example_value"]` with `or`. When `meta["val"]` is a tensor, that `or` evaluates the tensor's truthiness. As a result:
- A tensor with more than one element raises `RuntimeError: Boolean value of Tensor with more than one value is ambiguous`.
- A zero scalar is treated as missing, so the code falls back to a stale `example_value`.

This only shows up after `pass_propagate_shapes`, which runs FakeTensorProp and fills in `meta["val"]`. Any AutoSP pass that reads shapes after that step can hit it.

## Fix
Check `is not None` explicitly.

## Tests
Added `TestNodeShapeMeta` to `tests/unit/v1/compile/test_compile_autosp.py`. It covers:
- a multi-element tensor
- a zero scalar
- falling back to `example_value`

Before the fix, 2 of these tests fail. After the fix, all 3 pass.

Hardware: 8× Intel Arc Pro B70 (XPU), torch 2.14.0.dev+xpu, transformers 5.17. The rest of the AutoSP unit tests pass. `TestAutoSPCompile` is not counted: it fails the same way on master in this environment, in the Dynamo Ulysses baseline.

- A zero scalar is treated as missing, so the code falls back to a stale `example_value`.

This only shows up after `pass_propagate_shapes`, which runs FakeTensorProp and fills in `meta["val"]`. Any AutoSP pass that reads shapes after that step can hit it.

## Fix

## Tests
Added `TestNodeShapeMeta` to `tests/unit/v1/compile/test_compile_autosp.py`. It covers:
- a multi-element tensor
- a zero scalar
- falling back to `example_value`

Before the fix, 2 of these tests fail. After the fix, all 3 pass.

Hardware: 8× Intel Arc Pro B70 (XPU), torch 2.14.0.dev+xpu, transformers 5.17. The rest of the AutoSP unit tests pass. `TestAutoSPCompile` is not counted: it fails the same way on master in this environment, in the Dynamo Ulysses baseline.
detail.title: [AutoSP] Fix tensor truthiness in get_node_shape_meta

files.patch:
@@ -172,7 +172,12 @@ def find_node_by_name(gm: GraphModule, name: str) -> Optional[Node]:
 
 
 def get_node_shape_meta(node: Node) -> Optional[torch.Tensor]:
-    return node.meta.get("val") or node.meta.get("example_value")
+    # Compare with None explicitly: `or` would call bool() on the tensor, which raises for
+    # multi-element tensors and skips a valid zero-valued scalar.
+    value = node.meta.get("val")
+    if value is not None:
+        return value
+    return node.meta.get("example_value")
 
 
 def find_node_by_tag(gm: GraphModule, tag: str) -> Optional[Node]:

@@ -216,6 +216,29 @@ def test(self, seq_len):
             assert node.target == F.scaled_dot_product_attention
 
 
+class TestNodeShapeMeta:
+
+    # Shape propagation stores real tensors in meta["val"]; reading them must not depend on their truthiness.
+    @pytest.mark.parametrize("value", [torch.empty(2, 3), torch.zeros(())], ids=["multi_element", "zero_scalar"])
+    def test_prefers_val_over_example_value(self, value):
+        from deepspeed.compile.fx import get_node_shape_meta
+
+        node = Graph().placeholder("input")
+        node.meta["val"] = value
+        node.meta["example_value"] = torch.empty(4)
+
+        assert get_node_shape_meta(node) is value
+
+    def test_falls_back_to_example_value(self):
+        from deepspeed.compile.fx import get_node_shape_meta
+
+        node = Graph().placeholder("input")
+        example_value = torch.empty(4)
+        node.meta["example_value"] = example_value
+
+        assert get_node_shape_meta(node) is example_value
+
+
 class TestInputIdCompile:
 
     @pytest.mark.sequential
